plainTranslation: Obsessive, magnetic, all-consuming attraction. You bond at the root and the pull is enormous - and so is the possessiveness. It transforms how the Venus person loves, sometimes beautifully, sometimes through loss. Failure mode: jealousy, control, and the inability to let go when it's over. Magnetic and bad-for-you can be the same bond - name which one this is, and if it runs on control, that's not love.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep: Their intensity and pull toward depth and control sit right on top of your affections, tastes, and sense of worth. This is one of the closest contacts between you, strong and constant, energizing at its best and a lot to hold at its worst. Let the closeness feed you without letting it run you.
tension: But this aspect can become consuming quickly. The desire to be close can become the need to possess. Attraction can become obsession. The Pluto person may become controlling, jealous, or fixated on maintaining access to the Venus person. The Venus person may begin to feel dependent on the Pluto person's attention, approval, or desire. This is one of the clearest Venus-Pluto indicators of a bond that can be hard to leave when it is handled poorly. The intensity can feel like proof that the connection matters, even when the relationship is costing one or both people their peace.
advice: The distinction is simple: being wanted deeply is not the same as being loved well.
summaryShort: Their intensity and pull toward depth and control sit right on top of your affections, tastes, and sense of worth.
